newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS - Orogen PNG offer oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Orogen PNG offer oversubscribed.

text.p: The retail offer for Papua New Guinea residents of shares in Orogen Minerals Ltd closed on Wednesday heavily oversubscribed, joint lead manager and joint global co-ordinator McIntosh Securities (PNG) Ltd said.
McIntosh general manager John Hooton said details of the level of applications would be known on Thursday but indications were that initial targets had been exceeded by three times.
"The response from local clients, including many villagers, has been overwhelming," Hooton said. "There are boxes and boxes of applications that we have to count."
About 30 percent of the offer of 118.85 million shares has been set aside for PNG residents.
Orogen will have a stake in some of PNG's largest gold and petroleum projects, with the PNG government floating 49 percent of its Mineral Resources Development Corp (MRDC) through Orogen.
The main resource ventures in which MRDC and Orogen have interests are the Kutubu and Gobe oil fields and the Porgera, Misima and Lihir gold mines.

Hooton said that at last count late Tuesday there were over 3,000 applications from PNG residents worth about 22 million kina (US$16.5 million or A$21 million). He estimated an additional 30 million kina was received on Wednesday.
PNG residents were offered a discount price on the shares at 1.57 kina or 10 percent on the first 2,000 shares purchased and will be given the first preference in share allocations.
Australia and New Zealand investors were offered shares at A$1.57 each.
Orogen will list on the Australian Stock Exchange on November 1 after a A$261 million share raising.
The PNG government will retain a 51 percent stake in Orogen.
The institutional offer opens on Thursday and closes on October 30.
Jardine Fleming Ord Minnett partners McIntosh as lead manager and global co-ordinator.
